https://www.upi.com/Top_News/World-News/.text: France wildfires force mass evacuations from southwestern Gironde region July 24 (UPI) -- Authorities in France's southwestern Gironde region ordered tens of thousands of people to evacuate from the popular Cap Ferret peninsula vacation spot Friday in the face of an "XXL" wildfire threatening to cut off the promontory. As many as 2,000 escaped by boat. French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said 40,000 residents and tourists had been evacuated or were currently being moved from the cape, which is bordered by the Atlantic Ocean to the west and the Arcachon Bay to the east. The fire has burned through at least 25,000 hectares after breaking out Wednesday in Saumos, a small town about 25 miles away to the northeast. Authorities began evacuating of the town of Ares, south of Lege-Cap-Ferret on the Bay of Arcachon side of the peninsula after the fire picked up pace and intensity overnight, said fire and rescue chief Marc Vermeulen. A local council member said 2,000 people had already made the 7.5-mile boat crossing to Arcachon on the southern side of the bay. More than 800 firefighters from across France were battling the flames in an operation run out of a command center set up in a stadium in Le Porge, six miles northeast of Lege-Cap-Ferret. Gironda Prefect Sophie Brocas said 53 homes and a campsite had been razed but that firefighters had managed to save 2,000 houses. More than 23,000 people were also evacuated from homes, campsites, a nursing home and a summer camp due to another wildfire around Biscarrosse, about 15 miles south of Arcachon in the Landes department. Landes prefect Gilles Clavreul said the fire was being fueled by a combination of winds of more than 30 mph and searing temperatures in the high 30s degrees Celsius. Calling the situation very serious, President Emmanuel Macron said France had requested the European Union's civil protection mechanism be activated, which would allow the deployment of firefighting aircraft from other members of the bloc. "We will soon be able to count on reinforcements from two Croatian Canadair aircraft, two Portuguese Air Tractor planes, as well as two heavy Black Hawk helicopters from the Czech Republic and Slovakia," he wrote in a post on X late Thursday night. In Spain, authorities declared a national emergency Friday as they continued to battle three major wildfires west of Madrid in the areas of Villa del Prado and San Martín de Valdeiglesias, as well as Burgohondo in Avila province Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said Friday that many communities across Spain and beyond were being impacted by fires "ravaging thousands of hectares." "The government has deployed all available resources to halt the terrible fires that are currently affecting numerous areas: Avila, Leon, Toledo, Madrid, and other parts of Spain. We are living through a dramatic situation, not only in various Spanish provinces but also in regions of neighboring countries. Forest fires are ravaging thousands of hectares and affecting numerous communities," he wrote on X . "The government will stand by your side during the emergency and in the recovery," added Sanchez. He's currently a senior editor with experience in local and global coverage, and more than 1,000 test cars driven. He started his career at CarBuzz in January 2021. Sign in to your CarBuzz account Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google Discover Google News Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Whenever we talk about engines , us gearheads tend to focus on high-horsepower behemoths producing heart-rate-elevating power figures. Aside from that, discussions about engines are spurred on by a particular engine's quirks, applications, history, or significance to an automaker. We rarely highlight and discuss mundane engines that barely muster up more than 100 hp, which is even more true for diesel engines . However, today is an exception to the rule, so let's talk about a mundane diesel 'four,' called the Renault K engine. Despite its lack of grunt, it's proven to be an important mill that's helped motivate a wide range of vehicles in recent years, having been found in more than 50 different models since its inception. It was even used to power Mercedes-Benz models. A Brief Introduction To The Renault K Engine Renault K9K Diesel Engine Renault Referred to as the K-Type, this is an internal combustion engine family characterized by its inline four-cylinder design and has been produced by Renault since 1995. Typically, these engines followed the formula of four-stroke, four-cylinder engines with a water-cooled iron block, overhead camshafts, and aluminum cylinder heads. The K-Type engine was the successor to the Energy engine, an evolution of the Cléon-Fonte engine. The Energy engine, called the E engine, had the same specs and engine internals as the K-Type engine. So, Renault were hardly pushing the boat out when penning the K-Type, but why fix what wasn't broken in the first place? Compared to the other four-cylinder engines we've covered in the last two years, like Mercedes-AMG's prolific M139 four-cylinder engine , the Renault K-Type engine was nothing special. It was a standard engine used in standard production series vehicles. Two camps existed in the Renault K-Type engine family; one was gasoline, and the other was diesel. The latter is the focus of this article and was referred to as the K9K engine, a series of turbocharged diesel engines developed in collaboration between Renault and Nissan. The first K-Type engine appeared in the Renault Mégane, but production of the K9K engine began in 2001, and by 2013, more than 10 million engines had been produced and sold. While it was used in a myriad of passenger car models, none of which are considered the best diesel cars ever , the main application of the K9K engine was in Renault's MPV and hatchback models. Powering Renault's MPVs And Hatchbacks 2013 Renault Clio Exterior Yellow And Red Models Photographed Together Renault Going by many names, the diesel variant of the Renault K-Type engine was characterized by its 1.5-liter displacement, direct common-rail fuel injection system, a turbocharger supplied by Garret and BorgWarner, and some configurations of the K9K engine featuring a fuel injection system supplied by Delphi. Although only displacing 1.5 liters, it was far from the smallest diesel engine ever used for a mass-production application. It's worth noting that there were three versions of the turbo-diesel K9K engine: a low-output version, a high-output version, and a high-output version with a variable-geometry turbocharger. Remember, 'high' output here is relative to the low output version — even the most potent was a far cry from what you might consider an exciting engine. Outputs vary depending on emissions standards. For Euro 3 standards, outputs could be between 60 and 80 hp, while Euro 5 standards saw outputs range between 75 and 110 hp. It was far from being one of the most powerful diesel engines ever created , that honor going to the Ford 6.7-liter powerStroke V8, with Volkswagen's V10 TDI worthy of a special mention. Front shot of a brown 2016 Renault Kadjar Renault Several adjustments and refinements were made to the engine over its lifetime. Recent K9K homes include under the hood of Nissan's Juke, various Dacia models, and a smattering of small Renaults, like the evergreen Clio and Kadjar crossover. These adjustments included coating the tappets in the engine to reduce friction, revision of the injector spray angle, new piston rings, revising the injection pattern, and more, all to keep improving the efficiency of the K9K engine. In addition to the aforementioned more recent models, the K9K engine was used in the following Renault models: Mégane, Scala, Modus, Scénic, Kangoo, Fluence, andTalisman. Although many of these names might be unfamiliar to some, considering that Renault hasn't sold a model in the United States in decades, they are important models for other markets worldwide, and some markets have best-selling Renault models. However, Renault has ceased its ventures into new diesel engines and, in 2021, dropped its diesel engines from its lineup, another marker of the decline of diesel engines . The OM607 And OM608 Engines 2013 Mercedes-Benz-A-Class Hatch W176 Blue Front Angled View Mercedes-Benz When Renault and Nissan co-developed the K-Type engine, Mercedes-Benz was also involved. However, instead of adopting the K-Type engine into its fleet, a new engine would be created that was heavily based on the Renault K9K engine. Mercedes-Benz utilized two engines: the OM607 and the OM608. Both were turbocharged 1.5-liter inline-four-cylinder diesel engines. The former arrived first, characterized by its common rail fuel system, naturally aspirated design, different bearings, and a dual-mass flywheel. In its most powerful configuration, this bit-sized engine mustered a total of 110 hp and 192 lb-ft of torque. Mercedes-Benz employed this engine in its A-Class and B-Class models, but it eventually evolved and was replaced by the OM608 engine. This was a similar design to the OM607 engine, characterized by its cast iron engine block paired with aluminum alloy cylinder heads, and featured two valves per cylinder. Compared to the OM607, the OM608 engine had a higher power output but commanded the same torque output. As efficient and reliable as the little engine is, it still likely comes a shock to many a Mercedes-Benz owner to pop the hood and find a plethora of Renault logos on various pipes and other components. Still, that's the reality of this rather bizarre collaboration, with premium models like the A-Class and CLA-Class sharing various mechanical items with cheap and cheerful Renault products. Dacia, Nissan, And Suzuki 2009 Dacia Logan Engine Render Renault The engine wasn't exclusive to Renault's and Mercedes-Benz's ranks. Dacia, a Romanian automotive brand owned by Renault, extensively employed the K-Type engine in several models. Similar to Renault, Dacia's use of the K9K engine was not restricted to a single model or body style; it was offered in the automaker's Dacia Lodgy MPV, providing 110 hp and one of its most prolific models, the Dacia Duster crossover mustering up 100 hp. 2009 Dacia Logan Exterior Finished Dacia Other models that utilized the Renault K9K engine in Dacia's fleet included the Dacia Logan and Dacia Sandero, the latter of which was also available as a sort of soft-roader called the Stepway, with beefed-up bumpers and a lifted ride height. Suzuki would adopt the Renault K9K engine, but it would only be used for the automaker's Jimny model between 2006 and 2011. In contrast to Suzuki's single stint with the K9K engine, Nissan used the engine in several of its models. The most powerful Nissan model motivated by the bit-sized diesel unit is the Nissan Qashqai, with a total output of 115 hp. Other Nissan models powered by this diesel engine include the Note, Micra, NV200, Cube, Sunny, and the Tiida. Having first arrived on the scene in the mid 1990s, it's impressive to see just how long a life this otherwise insignificant little diesel engine has carved for itself. However, as emission standards become stricter and diesel options continue to dwindle , it was only a matter of time before the Renault K9K engine was laid to rest. https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/a.text: Protective fences are still in place around the worst affected areas of Amatrice, Italy almost a decade since the tragedy. Photograph: Crispian Balmer/Reuters View image in fullscreen Protective fences are still in place around the worst affected areas of Amatrice, Italy almost a decade since the tragedy. Photograph: Crispian Balmer/Reuters Italy Anger over slow pace of reconstruction in Italian town devastated by earthquake in 2016 As of April, two-thirds of planned public projects in Amatrice had yet to begin, rising to seven in 10 in hardest-hit areas Angela Giuffrida in Rome Sun 23 Aug 2026 03.00 EDT Last modified on Sun 23 Aug 2026 05.05 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A s people gather in Amatrice on Monday for a mass to mark the 10th anniversary of the earthquake that struck the hilltop town and several neighbouring communities, killing 303 and leaving thousands homeless, politicians and other public figures will pay tribute. But for many, their words will offer little comfort: 10 years on, much of Amatrice, whose historic centre was wiped out by the 6.0 magnitude quake, is still being rebuilt and more than half of its roughly 2,100 residents continue to live in temporary housing. “They will make a good show of it, bow their heads and say: ‘We did a lot,’” said Sonia Santarelli, the president of Comitato Civico 3e36, a grassroots initiative established soon after the disaster. “But nobody will put their neck on the line. They will say the reconstruction is going well … but how can that be when so many are in homes that are uninhabitable?” View image in fullscreen The mountain village of Amatrice, Italy was devastated by the earthquake that struck in August 2016. Photograph: Alessandro Di Meo/EPA A report published last week by ActionAid Italy highlighted severe delays in rebuilding Amatrice and other areas damaged by the earthquake. According to the findings, as of April 2026, construction on roughly two-thirds of the planned public projects had yet to begin, rising to seven in 10 in the hardest-hit areas. Some €4.85bn (£4.15bn) has been earmarked for the works, the report said. The earthquake struck in the early hours on 24 August 2016, its tremors felt as far as Rome. Santarelli, who owns an agriturismo , or farm stay, in the hamlet of Torrita close to Amatrice, recalled being woken by a loud blast and the sound of buildings collapsing. There was virtually nothing left of the hamlet, she said, but fortunately nobody there died. View image in fullscreen Amatrice before the earthquake on 21 May 2016 (top), after the earthquake on 25 August 2016 (middle), and nearly 10 years later on 18 July. Photograph: Google/Vantor and Pleiades © CNES 2026, Distribution Airbus D/Reuters Santarelli counts her blessings that she was not made homeless either. Comitato Civico 3e36, whose name references the precise time – 3.36am – the earthquake hit, was founded to defend the communities affected and to ensure citizens have a voice in the reconstruction process. Prefabricated housing villages were set up in 41 sites across the affected areas. The wooden homes are cramped and especially stifling in the heat. “The heat and humidity squelch you,” said Santarelli. Furthermore, they are undignified places in which to die, she claimed, owing to limited space restricting the easy movement of coffins. Residents have also complained that the rooms are too small for traditional wakes. Some of those displaced are still paying mortgages on homes that don’t exist any more. “You cannot make people live in these conditions for so long,” said Santarelli. “So much work still needs to be done.” Projects that have been completed in Amatrice include a school and a handful of buildings in the historic centre. Construction of a new hospital is nearing completion and could open in 2027, provided it is fully equipped and staffed. There are many explanations for the sluggish reconstruction. Matteo Renzi, the prime minister at the time of the quake, had pledged to rebuild the towns as they were . Renzi resigned at the end of 2016 after a referendum defeat and since then Italy has had five different governments, each appointing commissioners for the rebuild. As with previous major earthquakes, such as the one that hit L’Aquila in 2009, reconstruction has been mired by bureaucracy, legal disputes and the general complexity of rebuilding historic centres in mountainous areas. Much of the pressure falls on the mayor. Elected in 2021, Giorgio Cortellesi said reconstruction efforts were hampered by the Covid pandemic and then by a government eco-renovation scheme, which was intended to revive the post-pandemic economy but instead pushed up the cost of building materials and lured construction workers away to more profitable jobs in other parts of Italy . skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every day Sign up to Headlines Europe A digest of the morning's main headlines from the Europe edition emailed direct to you every week day after newsletter promotion View image in fullscreen The mayor of Amatrice, Giorgio Cortellesi, indicates one of the destroyed buildings nearly 10 years after the disaster. Photograph: Crispian Balmer/Reuters Cortellesi, an engineer who was determined to contribute to Amatrice’s revival after miraculously finding his two sons alive during a desperate search through the rubble in the dark, said the reconstruction has gathered pace over the past couple of years. However, there is “a significant housing emergency”, he acknowledged, exacerbated by construction firms renting out homes for their staff, in turn driving up rents for people who live there. He said the council is working to reclaim some of those properties. As for the prefabricated villages, which are nearing the end of their 10-year warranty, they will need to be dismantled and their residents moved into their rebuilt homes. “They will return to their homes, which will be the safest in Italy and the most energy efficient,” Cortellesi said, but without offering a timeline for completion. View image in fullscreen Those living in the prefab temporary homes in Amatrice say they are not unsuitable for long-term use. Photograph: © ActionAid Amatrice’s population has declined over the past decade, with many choosing to move elsewhere for better prospects. But there is also a resilience among those who have stayed. Sergio Pirozzi, who was mayor at the time of the calamity, is one of them. Within minutes of the earthquake striking, he captured the devastation in a few stark words : “Half of the town is gone.” A football coach, Pirozzi had been at a dinner marking the 50th anniversary of the local team a few hours before. “Of those who I was with that night, 36 died and there were others who lost their wives and children. It is not something I will ever overcome,” he said. And yet, despite also having to live with the delays and frustrations of rebuilding, Pirozzi’s attachment to Amatrice is undiminished: “For me, even today, this is the most beautiful place in the world.” Explore more on these topics Italy Europe Natural disasters Earthquakes features Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed World Europe US news Americas Asia Australia Middle East Africa Inequality Global development

https://www.politico.eu/article/france-t.text: Journalist Léa Salamé said she will temporarily step down from her role anchoring French public television’s primetime news broadcast, the 20h, while her romantic partner, the MEP Raphaël Glucksmann, runs for the French presidency. “The 20h is a strategic platform where interviews with the candidates and campaign reports will be among the highlights of the coming year,” Salamé said in an Instagram post on Monday announcing her decision. “Wherever the campaign takes place, I’ll step aside. Everywhere else, I am and will remain a journalist.” Since taking her seat in the anchor’s chair of the 20h on France TV, Salamé has faced questions over the potential conflict of interest if Glucksmann, who has long signaled his presidential ambitions, were to join the race to replace Emmanuel Macron next year. Glucksmann announced his candidacy Sunday on TF1, France TV’s main competitor when it comes to the evening news. Advertisement Advertisement Asked if he and Salamé, who have been together for more than a decade, discussed his potential candidacy, Glucksmann said he understood what his presidential bid meant “for my loved ones and especially my partner.” “As with any couple, when one person’s decision has such a strong impact on the other’s life, we had long conversations,” Glucksmann told TF1. Though France has a history of high-profile working journalists engaged in relationships with politicians, Salamé said at a parliamentary hearing in February that she would step aside if Glucksmann ran for president. And during the last two European elections, when Glucksmann led the center-left Socialist Party’s list, Salamé recused herself from political coverage while co-hosting public radio France Inter’s morning news show. Salamé said that her decision, which was taken in coordination with management, was “both obvious and difficult.” “Obvious, because it stems from the strict code of ethics I have always imposed upon myself,” she said. “Difficult, because I love the news program we have built together night after night for the past year.” Advertisement Advertisement

Trump personally dispatched the Central Intelligence Agency chief and kept trusted aides and military leaders who normally would have been briefed on the trip in the dark about the message he would deliver to senior Kremlin figures, U.S. officials said. Ratcliffe’s secretive journey, which included flying into Moscow in an unmarked U.S. C-17 military cargo plane from Latvia, sent European officials scrambling for information after news of the visit spread, some of those officials said. After being briefed, two European officials said the CIA director reinforced to his Russian intelligence counterparts that the U.S. remained committed to the North Atlantic Treaty Organization’s Article 5, which says that an attack on one member is considered an attack on all. The Wall Street Journal previously reported that Ratcliffe warned Russian officials not to attack NATO countries. Ratcliffe’s visit follows recent intelligence assessments showing Moscow might test the alliance’s resolve within a few years, the Journal previously reported. European officials, for example, have warned that Moscow has accumulated Ukrainian drones for a potential false-flag operation against eastern-flank states. Key Takeaways Ukrainian forces struck a Russian strategic bomber at the Engels-2 Airbase in Saratov Oblast, demonstrating Ukraine’s ability to strike heavily defended targets in Russia’s rear. * Russian budgetary challenges resulting from its costly war effort, Ukraine’s long-range strike campaign, international sanctions, and economic mismanagement are manifesting in concrete operational problems. * The Russian Ministry of Defense (MoD) will likely expand its access to Russians’ personal and medical information ahead of rumored involuntary reserve call-ups after the September 20 State Duma elections. * Russian forces conducted an intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) test launch as part of the Kremlin’s nuclear saber-rattling to project military strength. * Russia is portraying its Starlink-jamming electronic warfare (EW) system as a breakthrough capability as part of its cognitive warfare effort to dissuade the United States from granting Ukraine access to Starlink over Russian territory. * Ukrainian forces made limited tactical advances in the Kostyantynivka direction. * Ukrainian forces are conducting repeat strikes against Russian oil refineries to keep them offline. * Russia launched 164 drones against Ukraine overnight. Putin’s next move? Five Russian attack scenarios Europe must prepare for Target 1: Svalbard archipelago Target 2: Åland islands Target 3: Eastern Estonia Target 4: Gotland Target 5: Land bridge to Kaliningrad With almost all of the Baltic coastline now NATO territory, Russian planners face an acute challenge: in the event of direct confrontation with the Alliance, their use of Baltic waters and airspace is at grave risk, as is the survival of Kaliningrad as a Russian entity. The defense of St. Petersburg, now almost a NATO suburb, is also in question from the Russian perspective. For these reasons, the Åland islands represent an attractive target. 133 Their possession in time of war confers vital advantages to Russia, altering the strategic landscape in the Baltic region significantly. These include more defense in depth for St. Petersburg, an enhanced air defense zone in the northern Baltic, and a potential platform for surveillance and reconnaissance as well as anti-ship missiles and rocket artillery. A military operation to seize them would also punish Finland for joining NATO and, like Svalbard, pose a wrenching dilemma for NATO. Though clearly an act of war, as well as a striking violation of international law, an unopposed military occupation in time of peace would more likely than not result in diplomatic protests, but perhaps not a NATO military response. Russian leaders make no secret of their desire to reincorporate the Baltic states into the Russian Federation. On multiple occasions, Putin has asserted the right to intervene using military force to “protect” ethnic Russians living abroad, citing the return of the Baltics and other former Russian territories as a matter of “historical justice.” 169 Such talk is no mere rhetoric. Since Putin’s strident presentation at the Munich Security Conference in 2007, Russia has invaded Georgia (where Russian troops remain), occupied the Donbas, annexed Crimea, and invaded Ukraine, leading to hundreds of thousands of deaths and the destruction of entire cities. 170 What conditions could entice Putin to contemplate a sudden strike into Lithuania? US disengagement from NATO or withdrawal of troops from Europe, major conflict or tension with China that diverts US resources, an assessment that NATO would not respond, or internal challenges to the Russian regime requiring an external enemy could all factor into a decision to invade. The rise of right-wing, nationalist governments in Europe and a calculation that Russia should strike before NATO can harden its defenses in the Baltic region are also considerations. At least from the Russian perspective, some or all of these might apply in the near term, leading to a risk assessment that the potential gains of the venture outweigh the costs. At present, the war in Ukraine appears to be at a stalemate, with neither side likely to achieve a decisive victory. Should it harden into stasis, Russia can rearm and reequip its armed forces as Putin looks elsewhere in pursuit of his imperial ambitions. It has certainly reduced my wrinkles' bristolpost Bookmark Share What's On By Catherine Addison-Swan Senior Affiliates Writer Dayna Farrington 04:33, 17 SEP 2026 Bookmark Women have praised the serum as leaving their skin looking 'smoother' (Image: Getty) The colder months herald skincare season, with autumn and winter evenings offering the ideal chance to settle in and treat yourself to some pampering when our complexions require it most. And devotees of Liz Earle have discovered a method to secure substantial discounts on favourites from the bestselling brand. Among Liz Earle's most highly-rated products is the Superskin Advanced Lift and Define Serum , which contains acacia tree extract - a plant-derived collagen alternative - alongside skin firming actives and antioxidant-rich botanicals that the brand pledges will unveil "firmer, youthful-looking skin". Retailing at £52, Liz Earle maintains that this serum can diminish the visibility of fine lines and wrinkles, alongside uneven tone and texture. A complete 75ml bottle of the serum features in the new 24 Days of Liz Earle Advent Calendar , which debuted last month ahead of the festive period. This collection represents a considerable investment for any skincare aficionado with a price point of £175 - however, with 24 products contained within, this equates to each item, including the Superskin Serum, costing merely £7.30. Additional favourites from the Superskin collection featured in the calendar include the Superskin Moisturiser with Natural Neroli , priced at £48, the Superskin Eye Cream retailing at £45, and the Superskin Advanced Nourishing Cleansing Balm costing £39. Considering this four-piece skincare regime would cost shoppers £184 when purchased individually, this means the remaining 20 products within the advent calendar are essentially complimentary, as reported by Mirror . For those seeking a more affordable festive countdown, Liz Earle enthusiasts can also purchase the 12 Days of Liz Earle Beauty Advent Calendar , containing products valued at over £200 but available for £79. While this calendar omits the Superskin Serum, it features favourites from the brand's other popular ranges, from Cleanse and Polish to Skin Repair. liz earle advent calendar Get the 24 Days of Liz Earle Advent Calendar This collection contains more than £575 worth of beauty products, including the Superskin Advanced Lift & Define Serum worth £52 £175 Liz Earle Buy now Liz Earle isn't the sole beauty brand unveiling its advent calendar selection this autumn. At Boots, customers have been clamouring to purchase the new No7 24 Days of Beauty Advent Calendar, priced at £60 and brimming with skincare and makeup essentials worth over £240, from toner and night cream to lipstick and blusher. Charlotte Tilbury has also unveiled the Hollywood Beauty Wonderland Advent Calendar, carrying a £170 price tag and containing 15 products, from Pillow Talk favourites to a mini charm makeup bag. Valued at £325.50, this calendar arrives in a glamorous star-adorned gift box that can be repurposed for jewellery storage. Returning to Liz Earle, the Superskin Advanced Lift and Define Serum - obtainable for more than 80 per cent off within the 24 Days of Liz Earle Advent Calendar - has garnered numerous enthusiastic reviews from customers. One individual reported: "Been using this product for two weeks now and as a 71-year-old I wasn't expecting much but I am pleased with the improvements made. My skin looks smoother, more moisturised with more elasticity." Another buyer commented: "This product will definitely now be on my 'must-have' list in addition to my other daily essentials. I wasn't sure it could live up to the promises for my 68-year-old skin but it is fantastic. You can actually feel the lotion gently tightening the skin as it quickly absorbs. It has certainly reduced my wrinkles and my friends have commented on how very few I have for my age!" A look at everything that's included in the 24 Days of Liz Earle Advent Calendar (Image: Liz Earle) A third reviewer enthused: "So glad I purchased this. As a lady of a certain age I need a bit more oomph in my skincare. This is a perfect day serum for my combination skin and is not sticky under moisturiser. It absorbs really well and feels lovely on my skin. Will be repurchasing when I run out." Some believed there was scope for enhancement, with one critic noting: "The only thing for me is that the smell is a little harsh. Other than that perfect." While another user remarked: "I have deducted one star purely because I find that two pumps (as suggested) is not enough to include my neck area." Meanwhile, another reviewer commented: "This is the second bottle I've bought. Love the way it makes my skin nice and smooth before applying my makeup."
